outcome: Neurotransmitter biosynthesis related pathways in the gut microbiome
cohort: The study included 146 Chinese children, consisting of 72 with Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) and 74 typically developing (TD) children.
finding: Children with ASD showed significant alterations in faecal microbiome composition and functionality, including increased bacterial richness, altered composition, depleted neurotransmitter biosynthesis related pathways, and a persistent underdevelopment of the gut microbiota compared to TD children.
